grading_scale.0: Not relevant. A different subject, or shares only generic vocabulary with the question.
grading_scale.1: Marginally relevant. Same general subject area; useful background, but does not address what was asked.
grading_scale.2: Substantially relevant. Addresses the question and supplies a real part of the answer, or answers it for a closely related system, organism or condition.
grading_scale.3: Directly answers the question. The paper's own subject and findings address exactly what was asked.

design.ideal_ranking: best achievable DCG@10 from the judged pool for that question
design.judge: blinded; question, title and abstract only, with no system, rank or identifier shown

limitations.pooling: Only documents at least one system returned, plus each question's source paper, were judged. A relevant paper no system found cannot enter the ideal ranking, so every nDCG here is relative to the best of what was collectively retrieved. The effect is the same for every system compared.
limitations.oracles: openalex_best_of_both and openalex_oracle_any are upper bounds, not usable systems. They select the better mode per question and per metric, which requires knowing the answer beforehand.
limitations.precision_denominator: Precision@10 divides by 10 even when a system returned fewer than ten results, because empty slots are a cost to the reader. precision_of_returned is reported alongside it for anyone who prefers the other convention.
limitations.title_only_documents: 589 pooled documents had no abstract available and could only be judged on their title. These come overwhelmingly from records where OpenAlex holds no abstract text.
limitations.ungraded_returned_documents: A returned document with no identifier of any kind cannot be matched to a judged pool entry and therefore contributes no gain. In this run exactly one such record occurred, an OpenAlex catalogue stub whose entire title is "Open Access", with no DOI, no PubMed identifier and no abstract. It was returned for one question by two OpenAlex arms. Treating it as contributing nothing is the correct outcome rather than a scoring gap, since the record carries no retrievable content.

rbai_semantic__vs__openalex_combined_sem.label: meaning-based search, ours against the stronger OpenAlex semantic variant

rbai_semantic__vs__openalex_oracle_any.label: meaning-based search against the most generous OpenAlex oracle

rbai_hybrid__vs__rbai_semantic.label: hybrid against our own meaning-based mode

rbai_hybrid__vs__rbai_keyword.label: hybrid against our own keyword mode

rbai_hybrid__vs__openalex_best_of_both.label: hybrid against the OpenAlex two-mode oracle

rbai_hybrid__vs__openalex_oracle_any.label: hybrid against the most generous OpenAlex oracle

duplicate_rule.rule: A paper's second and later appearances in one ranked list score as not relevant (gain 0). Positions are unchanged; precision_of_returned keeps the number of slots returned as its denominator; the oracles are built from the corrected per-arm values. Hit@1, Hit@10 and MRR@10 come from target_rank, the first appearance, and do not change.
duplicate_rule.corrects: graded-relevance-final.json, which scored every slot with its paper's grade, so that two slots holding one paper both earned its gain against an ideal ranking built from unique papers.
duplicate_rule.paper_identity: the pool's alias table (union-find over DOI, PubMed id and normalised title), as for grading

holm_adjusted_p.method: Holm (1979) step-down adjustment within each metric family across the 9 comparisons, applied to the p-values as stored in comparisons; adjusted values are rounded to the same number of decimals as the unadjusted ones.

title_only_sensitivity.method: Documents judged on their title alone (pool items with title_only true) are removed from both the ranked list and the ideal ranking, and the list closes up beneath them (condensed lists; Sakai 2007, "Alternatives to bpref", SIGIR). A paper still scores once per list. Precision@10 still divides by 10. Oracles take the per-question best of their inputs' condensed values. Intervals are the main analysis's bootstrap (10,000 resamples over questions, seed 20260908). title_only_share is title-only slots over slots returned, repeated slots included. A returned record resolving to no pool document stays, with gain 0.
